One approved person-equivalent (`godk_pe`) = one unit of sewage pressure, whatever the plant treats, however it treats it, and wherever its effluent goes.

file_meta._what: bathing water stations, with annual quality 1991-2018

constructions_on_record: `wbid` is the water-body code the layer gives each station: a category imposed when the layer was compiled, by someone the file does not name. 227 stations with a scored year carry a `wbid` that matches no `ov_id` in the marine layer exactly.

`quality_91` … `quality_18` hold one class per station per year. The rule that makes a class, and who set it, are not in the file, and no copy of such a rule is pinned in this repository. The label set changes: "Excellent" appears 1991–2018; "Good" appears 2011–2018; "Good or Sufficient" appears 1991–2010; "Not classified" appears 1991–2018; "Poor" appears 1991–2018; "Sufficient" appears 2011–2018.
"Not classified" (437) and empty (2857) station-years are in the file; areas.py drops them.

steps.title: Each plant goes to the water body with the nearest boundary vertex, within 20 km
steps.imposes: A plant belongs to the water body owning the nearest kept boundary vertex (every 4th vertex, `STRIDE`; 368,981 kept), and to none if no vertex is found within `MAX_ASSIGN_KM` = 20 km. The search walks square rings of 0.05° grid cells out from the plant's cell, 4 rings at most, and stops after the first ring beyond its own cell in which it met any vertex. A cell is 0.05° of longitude wide, so east–west the 4 rings reach about 12.4 km at 56° N, not 20: a plant 12–20 km east or west of the nearest boundary is dropped as if it were beyond 20 km, and a nearer vertex in an outer ring can lose to a farther one in an inner ring. What the plant discharges into is not read; the layer has no column for it.

why.reason: Assignment is by nearest point on the marine boundary, via a grid hash over the 1.47 M boundary vertices, with the largest distance per layer and area recorded so a reader can see how firm the assignment is. Outfalls sit on land; bathing stations sit on the shore; dumping grounds sit in the water. One rule, one distance, no hidden choices. For the value 20 km itself: no reason recorded; its comment says only what it does ("beyond this a point belongs to no marine area").

why.reason: The cross-sectional estimate at the end is a cum hoc effect size and is labelled as one. It regresses a sewage-driven outcome (bathing quality) on sewage pressure (treatment-plant PE and rain-conditioned outfall density), across areas rather than across years, because the open data have more areas than they have years of comparable observation.
